subject: Science
title: Float and sink
objectives: Children will put objects in water and see which float or sink.
Children will say float or sink with support.
content: Putting objects in water to see which float and which sink, and making boats that float.
teachingActivities: Let children predict by saying or pointing; put each object in the water together and say "float" or "sink"; use large objects only; keep a tray of towels ready.
learnerActivities: Put objects in water, say float or sink and put a floating object on the water.
resources: A cork, a leaf, a plastic cup, a wooden spoon
A stone, a metal spoon, a key, a coin-sized large washer
assessment: Observe whether each child says float or sink after seeing an object in water.
expectedOutcomes: Says float or sink after seeing an object in water.
Puts a floating object on the water.

lessons.title: Things that float
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will see objects float on water and say the word float.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can pour and play with water and say wet and dry.
resources: A cork, a leaf, a plastic cup and a wooden spoon
lessons.starter: Put a leaf on the water and say "The leaf floats. It stays on top."
teacherActivities: Put each object on the water one at a time and say "It floats."
Let each child put one object on the water.
Push a floating object down and let it go.
Ask "What floats?" and point to the objects.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say float.
Child puts an object in the water and watches.
Child watches it come back up and says float.
Child points to floating things.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put each object on the water one at a time and say "It floats." Children: Children watch and say float.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child put one object on the water. Children: Child puts an object in the water and watches.
Step 3. Teacher: Push a floating object down and let it go. Children: Child watches it come back up and says float.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What floats?" and point to the objects. Children: Child points to floating things.

practical.title: Floating things
steps: Set up a clear basin on a mat.
Say "float" for each one that stays on top.
practical.safety: Use only objects larger than a child’s mouth that are not sharp. Keep water shallow and supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Put the object in the water together and say float.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find another floating thing in the room.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Puts an object on the water
lessons.conclusion: Take the objects out and dry them with a towel.
lessons.homeConnection: Float a leaf or a plastic cup in a bowl of water at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "see objects float on water and say the word float" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Float, float, float on top. Float, float, float.

lessons.title: Things that sink
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will see objects sink in water and say the word sink.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can pour and play with water and say wet and dry.
resources: A large smooth stone, a metal spoon, a large key and a large washer
lessons.starter: Drop a large stone in the water and say "Splash! The stone sinks. It goes to the bottom."
teacherActivities: Drop each heavy object in the water one at a time and say "It sinks."
Let each child drop a heavy object in the water.
Pick the object up and let children feel how heavy it is.
Ask "What sinks?" and point to the objects.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say sink.
Child drops an object and watches it go down.
Child holds the object and says heavy.
Child points to sinking things.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Drop each heavy object in the water one at a time and say "It sinks." Children: Children watch and say sink.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child drop a heavy object in the water. Children: Child drops an object and watches it go down.
Step 3. Teacher: Pick the object up and let children feel how heavy it is. Children: Child holds the object and says heavy.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What sinks?" and point to the objects. Children: Child points to sinking things.

practical.title: Sinking things
steps: Set up a clear basin on a mat.
Drop heavy objects in the water.
Say "sink" for each one that goes down.
practical.safety: Use only large, smooth objects that cannot be swallowed. Keep water shallow and do not let children put objects in their mouths.

differentiation.support: Drop the object together and watch it sink.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to guess before dropping each object.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Drops an object in the water
lessons.conclusion: Take the objects out and dry them with a towel.
lessons.homeConnection: Drop a spoon and a leaf in a bowl of water and see what happens.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "see objects sink in water and say the word sink" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Float or sink?
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will guess and test if objects float or sink.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can pour and play with water and say wet and dry.
resources: Six objects: three float and three sink
Two hoops or trays labelled float and sink
lessons.starter: Show a cork and ask "Will it float or sink? Let us find out."
teacherActivities: Hold up an object and ask the children to guess float or sink.
Put it in the water and watch.
Put floating things on the float tray and sinking things on the sink tray.
learnerActivities: Children guess with a word or point.
Children watch and say float or sink.
Child puts the object on the right tray.
Children say float or sink for each object.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Hold up an object and ask the children to guess float or sink. Children: Children guess with a word or point.
Step 2. Teacher: Put it in the water and watch. Children: Children watch and say float or sink.
Step 3. Teacher: Put floating things on the float tray and sinking things on the sink tray. Children: Child puts the object on the right tray.
Step 4. Teacher: Check each tray together. Children: Children say float or sink for each object.

practical.title: Test and sort
steps: Sort into float and sink trays.
practical.safety: Use large objects only and supervise closely. Keep the water shallow and wipe spills.

differentiation.support: Offer two objects and say the guess together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a new object and test it.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Will the cork float or sink?

expectedOutcomes: Guesses and tests float and sink
Sorts objects into float and sink
lessons.conclusion: Dry the objects and put them away.
lessons.homeConnection: Test float and sink with safe objects in a bowl at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "guess and test if objects float or sink" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Floating boats
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will make a boat and see that it floats.
successCriteria: Puts the boat on the water
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can pour and play with water and say wet and dry.
lessons.starter: Show a paper boat and say "This is a boat. Let us put it on the water."
teacherActivities: Show a boat made from foam or folded paper.
Put the boat on the water and say "It floats."
Let each child push their own boat with a gentle puff or hand.
Try a large leaf as a boat.
learnerActivities: Children look and touch.
Children watch it float.
Child pushes the boat across the water.
Child puts a leaf on the water and watches.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a boat made from foam or folded paper. Children: Children look and touch.
Step 2. Teacher: Put the boat on the water and say "It floats." Children: Children watch it float.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child push their own boat with a gentle puff or hand. Children: Child pushes the boat across the water.
Step 4. Teacher: Try a large leaf as a boat. Children: Child puts a leaf on the water and watches.

practical.title: Boat race
steps: Fill a long tub with water.
Gently blow or push the boats across.
practical.safety: Use a shallow tub and supervise closely. Remove boats and wipe spills afterwards.

differentiation.support: Hold the boat together and place it on the water.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to put a small toy on the boat.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What pushes the boat?
questions.expected: Our hand or a puff of air.

lessons.conclusion: Dry the boats on a towel and say "Boats float."
lessons.homeConnection: Make a boat from foil or paper and float it in a bowl.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make a boat and see that it floats" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 7 float and sink check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child describes objects in water.
successCriteria: Says float or sink after seeing an object in water
Puts an object on the water
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can pour and play with water and say wet and dry.
lessons.starter: Sing the float song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: float, sink and boats.
At each station ask "Float or sink?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child says float or sink.
Children dry hands and tidy.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: float, sink and boats. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Float or sink?" Children: Child says float or sink.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children dry hands and tidy.

practical.title: Float and sink stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station closely and keep water shallow. Wipe spills quickly.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one object.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to explain float and sink to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says float or sink after seeing; puts an object on the water; sorts floaters and sinkers.

questions.question: Can you put it in the water?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 7
Uses the words float and sink
lessons.homeConnection: Try float and sink at bath time.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child describes objects in water" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
